properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 10 at 5:50AM CDT until September 10 at 7:15AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Port Fourchon LA to Lower Atchafalaya River LA
out 20 nm...
Coastal waters from Port Fourchon Louisiana to Lower Atchafalaya
River LA from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 715 AM CDT.

* At 550 AM CDT, a cluster of severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts was located 20 nm east of Ship Shoal 198, or
23 nm south of Isle Derniers. The cluster of severe thunderstorms
were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels and oil rigs...and create suddenly higher waves.
Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The cluster of severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open
waters.
properties.instruction:
Strong winds will be dangerous for boaters or anyone near the water.
Boaters should avoid waterspouts and never try to navigate near them.
Make sure all on board are wearing life jackets. Seek shelter or move
to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 6:27AM EDT until September 10 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington OH
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Pike County in south central Ohio...

* WHEN...Until noon EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 625 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area, with high water in locations across a large portion
of Pike County. Between 4 and 7 inches of rain have fallen. Some
storms may produce additional rainfall later in the day.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Waverly, Piketon, Pike Lake, Kincaid Springs, Cynthiana, Beaver,
Lake White, Buchanan, Idaho, Elm Grove, Pike County Airport,
Givens, Omega and Linn.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

To report flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and submit
your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued September 10 at 5:12AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Chandeleur Sound...

At 512 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a cluster of strong
thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak
waterspouts. This cluster of thunderstorms is generally located along
a line extending from 9 nm southwest of Chandeleur Sound to 11 nm
northwest of Breton Sound, moving northwest at 10 knots.

Mariners can expect widespread gusty winds to around 30 knots, higher
waves and dangerous lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe
harbor immediately until this activity passes.

Brief, weak waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on
alert in case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot late-season conditions expected with high
temperatures up to 112 to 116 in Death Valley and the Colorado
River Valley; up to 105 to 110 in the Las Vegas Valley, Moapa
Valley, and Pahrump Valley.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ this morning to 8 PM PDT /8 PM
MST/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 10 at 4:10AM CDT until September 10 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING FOR
LOCATIONS IN NORTH DAKOTA SOUTH AND WEST OF THE MISSOURI RIVER AND
LAKE SAKAKAWEA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over much of western and
parts of south central North Dakota today ahead of an approaching
cold front. Temperatures are forecast to climb into the upper 80s,
with afternoon humiditity values as low as 13 percent. Winds this
afternoon are forecast to be westerly 15 to 25 mph with gusts to 30
mph. Due to the low humidity and breezy conditions with abundant dry
vegetation, critical fire weather conditions are expected this
afternoon into this evening for locations in North Dakota to the
south and west of the Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of North Dakota to the south and west of
the Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea.

* TIMING...From 1 PM CDT /noon MDT/ this afternoon to 9 PM CDT /8 PM
MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...Southwesterly around 20 mph with gusts to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity as low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 10 at 1:12AM MST until September 10 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 105 to
110 expected. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Gila Bend, Sonoran Desert Natl Monument, Tonopah Desert,
Gila River Valley, Kofa, and Southeast Yuma County.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water, and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 3:51PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Hydrologic Concerns:
* High water flowing down the Kuskokwim River, in combination with
storm surge pushing up the up river, could cause water levels to
rise between bankfull and minor flood stage.
* The highest water levels would occur if the downstream high water
flow, storm surge, and high tide all occurred simultaneously.

Potential Impacts:
* More likely scenario: Bankfull conditions with no flooding
expected.
* Worst case scenario: Nuisance flooding in low-lying areas.

Locations:
* Along Kuskokwim River, from Bethel south to Napakiak.
* Along Johnson River, from Nunapitchuk and Kasigluk south to the
Kuskokwim River.

Timing:
* Highest water levels will likely occur around high tide on Friday,
from about 11 AM through 4 PM.
* Strongest winds (south to southwesterly, gusting up to 30 to 45
mph) from about 4 PM Thursday through 4 PM Friday.

Next Steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED WATER LEVELS ALONG KUSKOKWIM AND JOHNSON RIVERS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 3:46PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

For communities along Kuskokwim River (Tuntutuliak):
* High water flowing down the Kuskokwim River, in combination with
storm surge flowing up river, could cause water levels to increase
as high as bankfull to minor flood stage during high tide.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide, which will
be from around 11 AM through 4 PM.

For communities along the coast (Kongiganak, Kwigillingok, Kipnuk,
Toksook Bay, Tununak):
* Strong onshore winds could bring the potential for coastal erosion
and minor coastal flooding in the worst case scenario. The more
likely scenario is that water levels will remain below 1 to 2 feet
above the normal highest tide, and no flooding will occur.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide on Friday,
from about 10 AM through 2 PM. Communities further north, like
Toksook Bay and Tununak, may see higher water levels during
Thursday's high tide as well.

Next steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 1:51PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Streams draining southern slopes of the Western Brooks Range.

Incoming rainfall from a atmospheric river will bring rainfall to the
southern slopes of the western end of the Brooks Range through
Friday.  Rainfall totals may exceed two inches in some locations and
cause significant rises on small streams.

The Kobuk, Noatak, and Wulik Rivers should also see rises from this
system into the weekend, but no flooding is expected.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 9 at 12:56PM PDT until September 11 at 12:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf. Abnormally high tides around 7 feet are expected in the
evening between 8pm and 10pm.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Santa Barbara
County Southwestern Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern
Coast, Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No
significant damage is expected. There is also an increased
risk of ocean drowning due to strong rip currents. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering southerly swell will create
hazardous rip currents and elevated surf conditions. Elevated
surf may also enhance any minor coastal flood impacts during
high tide.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 9 at 3:14AM PDT until September 10 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees above
normal during the day, with overnight lows also running 10 to 20
degrees above normal.

* WHERE...Bay Area and Central Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration. Impacts possible in some health systems and in
heat-sensitive industries. Hot conditions can cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.
